headline: SILVER HITS $61.07 AS PCE MISS SPARKS RALLY: WORLD SILVER SURVEY 2026 CONFIRMS SIXTH STRAIGHT ANNUAL DEFICIT AT 46.3 MOZ
snippet: Silver December futures opened at $61.07 per ounce on October 1 — up over $13.76 year-over-year and more than 100% since early 2025 — lifted by the below-consensus August PCE print that cut October Fed rate-hike odds from 70% to 38%. The World Silver Survey 2026 has confirmed a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit at 46.3 million ounces, driven by structural industrial demand from solar panels, EVs, AI data centres, and defence electronics that continues to outpace global mine supply, with COMEX inventories near historic lows.

headline: CHILE COPPER OUTPUT SINKS TO 15-YEAR LOW: AUGUST AT 369,500T, DOWN 12.8% AS CODELCO MINE COLLAPSE ADDS TO ESCONDIDA LOSSES
snippet: Chile recorded its lowest monthly copper production since February 2011 in August 2026, at 369,500 tonnes — down 12.8% year-over-year — after a mine collapse at Codelco drove the state producer's output down 25% in August alone to its lowest in over two decades, while disruptions at BHP's Escondida and Spence further eroded output. Full-year Chilean copper production could fall approximately 7%, well above the 2.6% decline previously forecast by state agency Cochilco, leaving the world's largest copper-producing nation supplying materially less metal into a market where spot copper held near $14,417 per tonne.

headline: DEUTSCHE BANK TARGETS COPPER AT $10/LB BY Q2 2027: US-CHINA STOCKPILING TO HOLD 71% OF GLOBAL SUPPLY BY YEAR-END
snippet: Deutsche Bank published a copper price target of $10 per pound ($22,050/t) for Q2 2027 — approximately 50% above current levels — driven by a strategic stockpiling race between the U.S. and China that Deutsche Bank estimates will leave the two countries collectively holding 71% of global copper supply by year-end 2026. The bank cited unencumbered copper inventories shrinking toward critical levels, accelerating pre-tariff buying into U.S. warehouses, and a structural supply deficit from years of underinvestment that no amount of short-term recycling can offset. For copper-focused TSX-V and ASX juniors, a 12-month $10/lb target from a major investment bank is the kind of price signal that historically translates into renewed institutional interest in pre-production development assets.

headline: U.S. URANIUM: ANFIELD ENERGY CLEARS COLORADO STATE REVIEW AT JD-8 — FEDERAL NEPA NEXT AS Q2 2027 RESTART STAYS ON TRACK
snippet: Anfield Energy announced October 1 that the Colorado Division of Reclamation, Mining and Safety approved the 28.3-acre permit area and set a $620,000 reclamation warranty for the JD-8 uranium-vanadium mine near Naturita, Colorado — completing state-level review and advancing the restart process to the Federal U.S. Department of Energy Uranium Leasing Program, which confirmed its Environmental Assessment template was accepted for NEPA review on September 29. The JD-8 is a past-producing underground mine in Colorado's historic uranium belt; Anfield targets a Q2 2027 restart pending permit issuance and DOE Mine Plan approval, adding both uranium and vanadium to the domestic U.S. critical minerals production pipeline at a time when Washington has directed $7.6 billion into domestic critical mineral projects since January 2025.

headline: STRIKEPOINT GOLD TARGETING OCT 6 CLOSE ON US$70M NEWMONT NEVADA DEAL: 10-FOR-1 CONSOLIDATION OCT 2, C$90M CASH SECURED
snippet: StrikePoint Gold Corp. confirmed October 1 that its ten-for-one share consolidation takes effect October 2 and the US$70 million cash acquisition of Newmont's Northumberland gold deposit in Nevada is on track to close October 6. The combined entity will control Northumberland's 4.43 million ounce gold resource — dormant for over 15 years — with approximately C$90 million in cash remaining after close to fund an aggressive development program, backed by a fully completed $190 million bought-deal financing. StrikePoint's acquisition of one of the largest undeveloped gold deposits in Nevada establishes a new development-stage vehicle positioned to benefit from the current gold price environment and the sector's structural preference for Nevada-jurisdiction assets.

headline: AMAROQ WRAPS UP 4,729M NANOQ GREENLAND DRILLING: 88% HIT VISIBLE GOLD, METALLURGY CONFIRMS 97-99% RECOVERY AT NALUNAQ FLOW-SHEET
snippet: Amaroq Ltd. announced October 1 the completion of its 2026 drilling programme at the Nanoq Gold Project in South Greenland: 4,728.9 metres across 33 holes, with approximately 88% intersecting visible gold and copper sulphides consistent with previous campaigns. Metallurgical test work by SGS Lakefield confirmed Nanoq mineralisation is amenable to processing at the existing Nalunaq gold mine facility approximately 130km away, with overall gold recoveries of 97-99% using the current flow-sheet — a critical infrastructure synergy that substantially de-risks project economics without greenfield processing capital. Assay results remain pending; beach landing and access track construction has commenced at site to support resource drilling and potential bulk sampling.

headline: MAXUS MINING HITS VISIBLE ANTIMONY IN 9 OF 11 HOLES IN BC'S SLOCAN DIVISION — PAST-PRODUCING ALPS-ALTURAS SITE, ASSAYS 8-12 WEEKS
snippet: Maxus Mining Inc. (CSE: MAXM) announced October 1 the completion of its inaugural 11-hole, 1,413.5-metre drill program at the Alturas West antimony project in British Columbia's Slocan Mining Division, intersecting visible antimony mineralization in 9 of 11 holes at the past-producing Alps-Alturas mine site. Assays have been submitted to AGAT Laboratories in Calgary, with results expected in 8-12 weeks. Antimony is a NATO-designated critical mineral essential for flame retardants, ammunition primers, and solid-state batteries; China controls over 80% of global supply following its 2024 export restrictions. A new BC discovery with 82% drill hit rate at a past-producer positions Alturas West as an early-stage supply chain diversification asset in a metal where North American production is essentially zero.

headline: GOLDSEEK: GOLD STOCKS AT MOST BULLISH SEASONAL ENTRY — AUTUMN RALLY HISTORY FAVOURS 'ACCUMULATE' DISCIPLINE INTO OCTOBER FOMC
snippet: Adam Hamilton's autumn seasonal analysis on GoldSeek places gold mining stocks at their most bullish seasonal entry point of the calendar year: historically, in bull-market years, gold has delivered its largest percentage gains between October and February driven by physical demand from Asia's harvest and wedding seasons and year-end institutional allocation, with gold stocks amplifying those gains through operational leverage to the gold price. The analysis maps the current October 2026 setup — gold consolidating near $4,150 after a September drawdown, miners trading at record-margin fundamentals but at P/NAV discounts — against the seasonal patterns of 2009, 2019, and 2023, years where similar pre-rally consolidation setups resolved with 25-40% GDX moves. For investors who endured September's 5.4% gold decline, the seasonal framework provides a calendar anchor for the Q4 accumulation thesis that the PCE miss and falling hike odds have now reinforced.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER MINERS POST 47% FCF MARGINS WHILE TRADING AT CYCLE DISCOUNT: AGNICO AT $3,020/OZ, NEWMONT AT $2,800/OZ
snippet: A Discovery Alert analysis of Q2 2026 producer fundamentals shows the ten largest gold producers collectively generated $8.4 billion in net income — the sector's second-best quarter ever — while simultaneously trading at multi-year discounts to bullion on a P/NAV basis. Agnico Eagle's Q2 realized price was $4,483/oz against AISC of $1,459/oz for a $3,020 per-ounce margin and $1.33 billion in FCF; Newmont realized $4,414/oz against AISC of $1,621/oz for a $2,800 margin and record Q2 FCF of $2.2 billion. Despite 47% sector-wide FCF margins, gold mining equities continue to trade as if gold will revert toward $3,000, creating what the piece calls a structural valuation paradox that has historically resolved — in both 2016 and 2019 — in favour of the equities once gold price volatility stabilised and investor sentiment rotated out of defensive ETF positioning.

headline: LITHIUM STOCKS FALL AS CHINA GOLDEN WEEK KILLS PRICE SIGNAL: SQM -1.8%, ALBEMARLE -1.7%, NO FUTURES TRADING UNTIL OCTOBER 8
snippet: Lithium equities gave back Tuesday's bounce on October 1 as China's Golden Week holiday removed the primary price signal for the week: SQM fell 1.83% to US$64.87, Albemarle lost 1.71% to US$105.78, and the LIT ETF shed 0.18%. Chinese lithium carbonate futures will not trade again until October 8, leaving producer shares without fresh pricing information from the world's dominant market. The vacuum comes as CATL's Jianxiawo mine — China's largest lithium operation — has had its Environmental Impact Assessment formally revoked, an escalation beyond the 'unresolved' status that has dominated recent reporting and one that Benchmark Mineral Intelligence says could push the site's return to full capacity into 2027 or beyond, materially undermining the surplus narrative that drove lithium's 22% price drop in September.
